item.title: PostgreSQL Sequence Resetting: Common Issues & Solutions
item.description:
“PostgreSQL Sequence Resetting: Common Issues & Solutions”

Encountering issues where your PostgreSQL sequence’s next value doesn’t align with your table’s current maximum ID after operations like data imports, deletions, or rollbacks is a common challenge. This misalignment can lead to duplicate key errors or gaps in your auto-incrementing IDs. Fortunately, PostgreSQL offers several robust methods to resynchronize your sequences with your table data. This post delves into various techniques and provides practical examples to address this.

item.title: SQL Server Identity Gaps Explained: Causes and Solutions
item.description:
“SQL Server Identity Gaps Explained: Causes and Solutions”

Encountering gaps in your SQL Server identity column sequences can be perplexing. This behavior, often observed after service restarts or specific transaction outcomes, stems from performance optimizations introduced in SQL Server 2012. Understanding these causes is key to implementing effective solutions.

One primary reason for these gaps is the default caching mechanism for identity values. For INT columns, SQL Server now reserves a cache of 1,000 values, and for BIGINT or NUMERIC columns, this cache size expands to 10,000. When the SQL Server service restarts, any unused values within this cache are effectively lost, leading to subsequent inserts starting from a higher number, thus creating a gap. item.title: What Is a Database? For Newbies
item.description:
A database is an organized collection of data, typically stored and accessed electronically from a computer system. Databases are designed to efficiently store, manage, and retrieve data. In modern computing, databases are used in virtually every application that deals with large amounts of data, from social media platforms to financial systems, e-commerce sites, and much more.

The primary purpose of a database is to store data in a structured way that allows users to query, update, and manage the information easily and efficiently.

item.title: What Is SQL? Let's Just Know about
item.description:
SQL (Structured Query Language) is the standard programming language used to interact with relational databases. It allows users to perform various database operations such as querying, inserting, updating, and deleting data. SQL is used in nearly every database management system (DBMS), including MySQL, PostgreSQL, Microsoft SQL Server, and Oracle, making it an essential skill for anyone working in data science, software development, or database administration.

SQL enables developers and analysts to communicate with databases, retrieve specific data, and manage the structure of databases, all without needing to write complex programs.

item.title: How To Deal With Sql Server Restoring State
item.description:
FAQs on How-to-Fix-Database-Stuck-in-Restoring-State-in-SQL-Server

This guide provides practical solutions for when an SQL Server database is stuck in the “Restoring…” state. We’ll explore common causes, offer troubleshooting commands with detailed explanations, and provide alternatives to standard SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) methods.

What Causes SQL Server Databases to Get Stuck in “Restoring…” State?

A database may enter the “restoring” state if a restore operation was incomplete, a transaction log wasn’t applied, or there was an interruption. In such cases, SQL Server views the database as pending further recovery, causing it to remain inaccessible until the necessary recovery or transaction steps are completed.
